title: This Rare Porsche 924 Is Really Rally Good

body_markdown:
Think of the Porsche motorsport greats and what comes to mind? Most likely it’s the 19 outright wins at Le Mans in cars such as the 917, 962, 911 GT1, or the 919. It could be the 600 victories in IMSA and the 21 top steps on the 24 Hours of Daytona podium. It might even be all the “giant-killing” victories the firm achieved in its early days, with cars like the 550 Spyder and 718 RSK.


Chances are that rallying has gone rather under the radar, as Porsche only managed to secure a single world title in the discipline, in 1970. The techfest[959](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/porsche-959-driving-the-fastest-car-of-1985/) was effectively too late for the Group B era, but it did bag a couple of big wins in the 1985 Pharaohs Rally and, most notably, in the Paris-Dakar a year later.


Yet, even though Porsche has been letting loose on the world’s rally stages since the 1950s, and more recently reminded us with its Dakar models, the company’s rallying pedigree is oft forgotten.


That’s certainly true of the 1980 924 Turbo GT, chassis 0001, currently listed on[Hagerty Marketplace](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1980-Porsche-924/6VDkIMjoNRHORiLM80YJ40) .


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


The car was a pet project of Jürgen Barth, winner of Le Mans in 1977 and head of Porsche’s *Kundensport* (customer racing department). Barth worked closely with the engineers at Zuffenhausen to develop a competition version of the E831 2-liter inline four-cylinder engine. This was a motor sourced from VW/Audi, but handbuilt for racing and fitted with both a turbocharger and intercooler. The main event for the 924 was to be Le Mans, where three cars were entered, and Barth and Manfred Schurti finished a creditable sixth overall and third in class, but Barth was also given a car to take to the mountains above Monaco.


Broad Arrow


It was it “the forerunner of the new homologation car,” according to Barth, who had no idea how it would actually perform.


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


Broad Arrow


To ready it for rallying, the 924 got a new KKK K26 turbo, a G31/01 five-speed transmission and modified clutch, plus raised suspension to cope with the rough roads of the Monte Carlo Rally. Painted in plain white and adorned with Hugo Boss sponsorship, the car was ready in the nick of time and Barth took the start, along with 236 other competitors. Over a 430-mile route, with almost 200 miles of special stages on a mix of asphalt, snow, and ice, Barth and co-driver Roland Kussmaul came home in 19th place overall and sixth in class. A year later, the pair tried again but were only able to finish in 96th place.


Broad Arrow


Barth retired the 924 but kept it in his personal collection for the next 40 years, until it was sold to its current keeper in 2022. Over the decades it has been displayed in museums across the world, a testament to Porsche’s early turbocharging efforts and a proof of concept that led to the 924 Carrera GTR endurance racer and the road-going[924 Carrera GT](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/porsche/924/1981/1981-porsche-924-carrera_gt?id=aCn1I000000Cy3CSAS) . In the years since Monte Carlo, however, it has seen little action, so it would require reconditioning before it hits a road or rally stage again.


The car still wears its competition battle scars and is sold with a sheaf of historic documentation and photographs, plus two helmets won by Barth and Kussmaul. It comes with a clean Montana title, and its original German registration. It is being sold with no reserve, and the auction ends on September 30.
